memory_update.text: Highest-priority direct US-listed node candidates for AI networking/optical interconnect: AVGO, MRVL, ANET, COHR, CRDO.

The node decomposes into at least five investable public-market sublayers: Ethernet/switch ASICs, AI networking systems, optical DSP/coherent DCI, lasers/InP/silicon photonics/transceivers, and AEC/retimer/high-speed electrical connectivity.

Not included due to five-candidate limit but should be considered in later passes: NVIDIA networking/Spectrum-X, Astera Labs, Lumentum, Fabrinet, Amphenol, TE Connectivity, Corning, Applied Optoelectronics, Cisco, HPE/Juniper, Innolight and Eoptolink ADR/accessibility checks.

Need follow-up evidence pass to separate real AI exposure from data-center adjacency: quantify revenue tied to 800G/1.6T optics, CPO, AI Ethernet, custom AI ASICs, AECs and retimers; identify customer concentration and volume shipment status.
COHR should be tracked as a vertical photonics candidate for AI networking, with emphasis on InP, EMLs, photodiodes, 800G/1.6T transceivers, silicon photonics, and CPO.
LITE should be tracked as an EML/laser and datacom transceiver candidate; next validation should focus on whether EML or laser capacity is truly scarce versus merely high demand.
FN should be tracked as a second-order optical manufacturing capacity candidate rather than an optical IP owner; evidence needs customer/product-level AI exposure.
CRDO should be tracked as a high-speed copper/optical connectivity and AEC/DSP/retimer candidate for AI cluster fabrics.
CLS should be tracked as a 1.6TbE AI switch-platform and integration supplier tied to Broadcom Tomahawk 6 adoption.

Next Layer 1B pass should separately evaluate US-listed test/measurement and inspection suppliers for 800G/1.6T optics, including VIAV and Keysight, plus silicon photonics foundry/platform candidates such as GFS and Tower Semiconductor.
This pass did not include non-US primary listings such as Innolight and Eoptolink despite strong node relevance; they should be captured in a non-US or ADR/global-listings pass.
Add Celestica (CLS) as a second-order AI networking candidate: ODM/platform supplier for 1.6TbE and 102.4T AI switching systems using Broadcom Tomahawk 6.

Add Ciena (CIEN) as an adjacent AI optical interconnect/DCI candidate: stronger for scale-across and DCI than intra-rack GPU fabrics, but relevant through WaveLogic 6 1.6T, CPO, and data-center interconnect products.
Add Lumentum (LITE) as a component chokepoint candidate around lasers, CW lasers, EML/DML, 800G/1.6T transceivers, silicon photonics, and CPO architectures.
Add Credo (CRDO) as a direct AI connectivity candidate spanning AECs, retimers, optical DSPs, SerDes, 800G/1.6T products, and silicon photonics via DustPhotonics.
Add Astera Labs (ALAB) as an adjacent rack-scale AI connectivity candidate; key exposure is PCIe/CXL/Ethernet signal integrity and reach rather than classic optical transceiver/module supply.

Not included due to five-candidate cap but worth later passes: Coherent (COHR), Fabrinet (FN), Amphenol (APH), TE Connectivity (TEL), Corning (GLW), Cisco (CSCO), Marvell (MRVL), Broadcom (AVGO), Arista (ANET), Nokia ADR (NOK), and Viavi (VIAV).
